page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 12 virtual CPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 48.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. This instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng yield scores of 1575.58 and 12474.34 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 698.22 GB/sec, though large block uncached read and write speeds drop to 55.6 GB/sec and 46.36 GB/sec. The instance exhibits weak performance in PassMark physics and memory tests, but maintains average throughput in database operations and Redis SET operations, which reach 11.64 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, prompt processing with a small 135M LLM model reaches 755.34 tokens per second, but drops significantly to 17.38 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

Given its dedicated Intel Xeon processor and balanced resource allocation, the ecs.cm4.3xlarge offers a stable, predictable environment for general-purpose workloads without the risk of resource contention. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which should be factored into overall architecture planning. This instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text and image processing, and moderate database operations. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference due to its average memory bandwidth and weak performance on larger models.
